about.subtitle: People · Work · Opportunities — a trusted bridge between Azerbaijan and Germany.
about.story:
Triad Vision was founded to connect talented, hard-working people in Azerbaijan with German companies that need skilled workers. Our mission is to build legal, transparent and long-term cooperation for both sides.

Our team works in Baku and Germany and directly manages every stage, from candidate selection to the first day at work.

page.title: Accessibility statement
page.lead: We build the Triad Vision website and client portal so that everyone can use them comfortably – including people with visual, hearing, motor or cognitive impairments.
page.goalText: We aim for conformance with WCAG 2.1 (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) level AA. The site is reviewed regularly and issues are fixed as they are found.
measures: Full keyboard navigation: every menu, form and dialog works with Tab, Enter and Esc; a "Skip to content" link is the first element on every page.
Colour contrast of at least 4.5:1 between text and background, plus a high-contrast and a dark mode.
Text can be enlarged up to 150%; line spacing, letter spacing and a readable font are available.
Read-aloud mode: the element under the pointer or in focus, and the whole page, are read with the browser voice.
For screen readers: semantic HTML, ARIA labels, a proper heading hierarchy and alternative text for images.
Animations can be stopped; the operating system "reduce motion" setting is respected automatically.
All information is textual – there is no audio or video content; support is available in writing.
The site is offered in 4 languages (Azerbaijani, German, English, Russian) and the page language attribute is set correctly.
limits: Most browsers have no speech-synthesis voice for Azerbaijani; read-aloud falls back to a Turkish or English voice.
Some third-party documents (PDF) may not be fully accessible – on request we send a text version.
page.contactText: If you have difficulty using any part of the site, write to us – we will respond as soon as possible and provide the information in a format that works for you.

svc.title: The whole process, from search to arrival
svc.subtitle: Click a service to see what is included and how it works.
svc.askText: Fill in the form and your manager will contact you within 24 hours.

process: In the first meeting we learn about your profession, experience, language level and goals. For companies we define the job profile together. At this stage we determine the right visa type.
A personal document checklist is created in your account. You upload documents online, we check each one and ask for corrections if needed. We also help with translation and certification.
We arrange a meeting with a matching employer. Once agreed, the contract is sent to your account and you sign it electronically on screen. Both sides get the signed PDF immediately.

The embassy document package is prepared, Federal Employment Agency approval is obtained and the embassy appointment is booked. We prepare you for the interview and notify you of every change until the decision.
Once the visa is approved we plan the flight, pick you up at the airport and settle you into your housing. We help with registration, a bank account and insurance.
From your first working day you and your employer have a dedicated contact person. We stay in regular contact in the first months and solve questions quickly.
why: We only work with official visa types: §18a, §18b, §19c, §16a, §16d and seasonal work. Every contract is checked against German labour law, with no hidden fees.
In your account you upload documents, sign the contract, track the status and message your manager. You get a portal and email notification at every step.
Every candidate and company gets a dedicated manager, so you always know who to contact.
With complete documents, embassy processing usually takes 3–8 weeks. The fast-track procedure (§81a) can shorten it further.
Our team speaks Azerbaijani, German, English and Russian. The website, account and notifications are available in all 4 languages too.
We are there after the visa as well: airport pick-up, housing, registration, bank, insurance and onboarding.

checklist.germanNeeded: Bring your German up to at least {{level}} and take a certified exam (Goethe, telc, ÖSD).
checklist.germanOk: Your German level is sufficient — keep your language certificate ready.
checklist.germanNursing: Nursing requires at least B1 German, and B2 for full recognition.
checklist.truckLicence: Get a CE licence and code 95 (driver qualification) — both are mandatory for truck drivers.
checklist.truckCode95: Have your code 95 confirmed in Germany and your licence converted.
checklist.driverCard: You will need a driver card (Fahrerkarte) for the digital tachograph.
checklist.licenceConvert: Your licence must be converted into a German one within 6 months.
checklist.courierLicence: Courier work requires at least a category B driving licence.
checklist.nursingRecognition: Apply for recognition (Anerkennung) of your nursing diploma — an adaptation course or knowledge test may be required.
checklist.schoolCertificate: Prepare your school certificate with an apostille and certified translation.
checklist.ausbildungAge: Ausbildung mainly targets younger applicants — after 35 it is harder to find a place, so consider alternatives too.
checklist.ausbildungFunds: You must prove you can support yourself — through the training salary or a blocked account.
checklist.seasonal: Seasonal work permits are time-limited — apply a few months before the season starts.
checklist.degreeAnabin: Check that your degree is recognised in the anabin database — important for the Blue Card.
checklist.itDegree: A visa is possible without a degree too: with 3 years of IT experience within the last 7 years.
checklist.qualificationNeeded: This field requires vocational training or a documented qualification — a short professional course can help.
checklist.recognition: Have your qualification checked for recognition in Germany (Anerkennung) — we help with the paperwork.
checklist.experienceBuild: At least {{years}} years of documented experience in this field will strengthen your profile considerably.
checklist.experienceProof: Prove your experience with your employment record book and employer references.
checklist.age45: From age 45, a first work visa requires a minimum salary or proof of pension provision.
checklist.passport: Have a passport ready that is valid for at least 12 more months.
checklist.cv: Prepare a CV in the German format (Lebenslauf).
